name: Pius XII
role: Pope of the Roman Catholic Church 1939-1958 (born Eugenio Pacelli, 1876-1958)
summary: Pius XII taught that State authority is bounded by natural law, that the human race is one, that wars of aggression must be banned by an international authority with real power, and that the Church accepts any form of government capable of securing the common good, including democracy; he condemned relativism and polygenism.

notFound.work: His wartime conduct and the 1933 Reichskonkordat as acts

tried.how: Gutenberg, the reference library and Miller Center hold nothing about the acts; the Vatican site carries his words, not records of the acts
not pursued: the acts are contested in the historical literature and a reference account alone would only support a low-confidence answer

abortion-legal.rationale: Told the midwives in 1951 (Italian; my translation) that 'the direct killing of the child as a means' is not lawful even to save the mother's life, and that 'the life of an innocent is untouchable, and any direct attempt or aggression against it is a violation of one of the fundamental laws'.

assisted-dying.rationale: Held in 1951 (Italian; my translation) that 'the direct destruction of the so-called life without value, born or unborn' cannot be justified and that 'the life of an innocent is untouchable'; he spoke of direct killing, not of the terminally ill by name.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Told China's Catholics that their Church 'will not be able to be ruled with autonomy of government' but must be 'completely subject to the Supreme Pontiff'; bishops' jurisdiction 'flows... only through the Successor of St. Peter', not from a national body.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: In 1941 (Italian; my translation) he recalled Leo XIII's admonition that the State has a duty 'to apply itself to social providence, caring for the well-being of the whole people and all its members, particularly the weak and disinherited, with a broad social policy and the creation of a labour law', and called it a 'sincere debt of justice' to acknowledge the progress made.

democracy-best.rationale: Wrote that 'it is not forbidden to prefer temperate, popular forms of government' and that the Church 'does not disapprove of any of the various forms of government, provided they be per se capable of securing the good of the citizens'; neither preferring democracy as best nor rejecting it.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: In his 1944 Christmas message he said of a future society of peoples that 'the authority of such a society must be real and effective over the member states, in suchwise, however, that each of them retain an equal right of its own sovereignty'.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Wrote that 'the human race' has 'one common origin in God', 'the unity of nature which in every man is equally composed of material body and spiritual, immortal soul', and quoted 'where there is neither Gentile nor Jew... bond nor free'.

family-wage.rationale: Wrote that 'the salaries of the workers, as is just, are to be such that they are sufficient to maintain them and their families', quoting Pius XI that fathers must receive 'a wage sufficient to meet adequately normal domestic needs' and that social justice demands reforms that 'guarantee such a wage to every adult working man'.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Wrote in 1951 (Italian; my translation) that direct sterilisation 'is a grave violation of the moral law and is therefore illicit', that 'public authority has no right, under pretext of any indication, to permit it, much less to prescribe or have it carried out against innocents', and that killing, even by order of public authority, those who 'for physical or psychic defects are not useful to the nation' is forbidden by natural and divine law.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Named 'the right to a character and a culture of its own' among the rights of peoples in 1953 (Italian; my translation); he spoke of peoples and States, not of minorities within a State.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Wrote in 1953 (Italian; my translation) that each State 'is immediately subject to international law, and thereby to the natural law', so that it 'is no longer - nor has it ever been - sovereign in the sense of a total absence of limits'.

national-self-determination.rationale: Listed among the requirements of the natural law of nations (1953, Italian; my translation) 'the right to existence, the right to respect and good name, the right to a character and a culture of its own, the right to development', for each people and State, and rejected world empires in which peoples are 'fused, willing or unwilling, into a single state complex'.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Wrote that 'the rich, if they are upright and honest, are God's dispensers and providers of this world's goods' and that 'if the rich and the prosperous are obliged out of ordinary motives of pity to act generously towards the poor their obligation is all the greater to do them justice'; God 'does not wish that some have exaggerated riches while others are in such straits that they lack the bare necessities of life'.

person-over-state.rationale: In the 1942 Christmas message (Italian; my translation) he listed the fundamental rights of the person that a juridical order must protect, whose 'function is not to dominate but to serve', and rejected any materialism that 'sees in the people only a flock of individuals'.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: In the 1953 address to Catholic jurists (Italian; my translation) he described a 'juridical community' in which 'the states, remaining sovereign, freely unite', 'an ascent from below upward, from a plurality of sovereign states towards the highest unity', and called a supranational legal community of peoples rooted in 'the unity of their origin, their nature and their end'.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Wrote that the Church 'cannot and does not think of deprecating or disdaining the particular characteristics which each people, with jealous and intelligible pride, cherishes and retains as a precious heritage', and that nations are meant to 'enrich and embellish' the unity of the human race.

property-fundamental.rationale: In the 1941 Pentecost message (Italian; my translation) he wrote that 'nature itself has intimately joined private property with the existence of human society and... the family', and that State rules should not through 'excessive burdens or interference' make private property 'empty of meaning'; but that property 'remains subordinate to the natural purpose of material goods' and cannot be independent of the primary right of all to their use.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: In 1941 (Italian; my translation) he held that 'the original right to the use of material goods' is the basis, to which private property 'must serve to make its realisation possible', so that property and use of goods bring 'fruitful peace' to society, not 'conditions generating strife and jealousy'.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: In Sertum Laetitiae he said that if a family-sufficient wage is not always feasible 'social justice demands that reforms be introduced without delay which will guarantee such a wage to every adult working man'; he named no legal minimum.

reason-over-faith.rationale: In Humani Generis he warned against philosophies that 'repudiate all that is absolute, firm and immutable' and held that 'the sources of revealed truth' bind inquiry, as on polygenism, where 'the children of the Church by no means enjoy such liberty'.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Asked 'by what right can men arbitrarily and diversely in different nations, interpret the gospel of Jesus Christ?', allowing adaptation of the manner of preaching to a people but not of the doctrine; in Humani Generis he condemned philosophies that 'repudiate all that is absolute, firm and immutable'.

restrict-conversion.rationale: In 1953 (Italian; my translation) his words point both ways: error 'has objectively no right to existence, to propaganda or to action', which leans toward legal restriction in principle, but 'the duty to repress religious and moral deviations cannot be an ultimate norm' and a Catholic statesman may justify not preventing it by State law 'in the interest of a higher and wider good', a prudential exception; he did not discuss conversion by name.

separate-church-state.rationale: Condemned ideas which 'divorce civil authority from every kind of dependence upon the Supreme Being' and 'from every restraint of a Higher Law derived from God', holding that State and morals cannot be severed from religion.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Condemned the error that would 'divorce civil authority from every kind of dependence upon the Supreme Being' and 'from every restraint of a Higher Law', so that the State 'attribute[s] to itself that absolute autonomy which belongs exclusively to the Supreme Maker'.

state-harmful.rationale: In 1944 he wrote that 'the state also' belongs to the absolute order of beings 'as a necessary society endowed with authority, without which it could neither exist nor live', and that the democratic state 'should be entrusted with the power to command with real and effective authority'.

strong-leader.rationale: In the 1944 Christmas message he reported, as a development he found understandable, that the peoples were 'more aggressive in opposing the concentration of dictatorial power that cannot be censured or touched' and 'call for a system of government more in keeping with the dignity and liberty of the citizens'; he did not state the point as his own conclusion.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Wrote that 'by the same Divine Will, the people or the civil authority must not invade the rights and the constitution of the ecclesiastical hierarchy', rejecting a Church governed by or autonomous within the nation.

total-state.rationale: Wrote that when civil authority denies God's law it 'puts itself in the place of the Almighty and elevates the State or group into the last end of life, the supreme criterion of the moral and juridical order'.

traditional-family.rationale: In the 1941 Pentecost message (Italian; my translation) he wrote that 'in the family the nation finds the natural and fruitful root of its greatness and power', a function 'in the natural order in some respects superior to every other'; the use of goods, work and the family are the three fundamental values of social life.

unions-good.rationale: In Sertum Laetitiae he wrote that 'it is not possible without injustice to deny or to limit either to the producers or to the laboring and farming classes the free faculty of uniting in associations by means of which they may defend their proper rights'.

universal-morality.rationale: Lamented 'the denial and rejection of a universal norm of morality as well for individual and social life as for international relations' and 'the forgetfulness of the natural law itself, which has its foundation in God'.

widespread-small-property.rationale: In the 1942 Christmas message (Italian; my translation) he wrote that 'human dignity requires as a natural foundation the right to the use of the goods of the earth, to which corresponds the fundamental obligation to grant private property, if possible to all', and that law must stop the worker from being 'condemned to an economic dependence and servitude' whether by private capital or by the State.

notes: Read by theme on the Vatican site: Summi Pontificatus (1939), the Christmas message of 1944 and Humani Generis (1950); Sertum Laetitiae (1939) and the Italian originals of the 1941 Pentecost message, the 1942 Christmas message and the 1951 address to midwives were read by theme (translations mine); Mystici Corporis Christi (1943), Sacra Virginitas, Evangelii Praecones and Divino Afflante Spiritu were fetched but not used for any answer. Thirty-four statements answered, all from his own words; his wartime acts and the Reichskonkordat (negotiated as Secretary of State, 1933) are not used. The uncertainty rule is not met.
